facts.statement: New records are built with id `bm-${crypto.randomUUID()}`, hostname from getHostname(url), and defaults visitCount=0, visitedAt=null, isPinned=false, isArchived=false, createdAt=Date.now(); edits preserve the previous id, isPinned, isArchived, visitCount, createdAt, and visitedAt.
Pin/Unpin and Edit actions are rendered only when the item is not archived, and Edit loads the item's url/title/description/tags/favicon into the dialog.

The Valibot BookmarkFormSchema requires a non-empty URL matching /^https?:\/\/(?:[\w-]+\.)+[a-zA-Z]{2,}(?:\/\S*)?$/ and v.url, a non-empty title up to 100 chars, a non-empty description up to 280 chars, and 1-5 tags each up to 30 chars.

The scenario's user-controlled 'category' (归类) is realized only as up to five free-text tags on each record; there are no creatable, renameable, or nestable collections, and no separate move operation beyond editing tags.
saveBookmark sets the record in the in-memory map then awaits db.bookmarks.put(bm); deleteBookmark removes from the map then awaits db.bookmarks.delete(id).
A Delete action is rendered only for archived items; it calls deleteBookmark and shows an error-type toast with an Undo action that calls saveBookmark(item) to restore the record.
The scenario step of letting unclassified links land in a default category is not supported, because the form schema rejects saves with zero tags.
A Copy URL action writes item.url to the clipboard and shows a success toast.

Metadata and favicon enrichment is best-effort and dependent on third-party HTTP services; failures degrade silently to console errors while the bookmark still saves with whatever fields the user entered or omitted defaults for.
An effect on component creation calls db.bookmarks.toArray() and inserts each returned bookmark into an in-memory RippleMap keyed by bookmark id.
On submit, if no favicon exists and a hostname is derivable, the code fetches a Google s2 favicon proxied through images.weserv.nl inside a try/catch that only logs failure.

Persistence is local to one browser profile/device via IndexedDB with no sync layer, so the scenario's cross-session growth holds only on the same browser, and the leaf's multi-device context is unmet.
Deletion is limited to archived records and recovery is only the transient Undo action on the toast; there is no trash view, and non-archived records cannot be deleted at all through the UI.
The Visit action builds an updated bookmark with visitedAt=Date.now() and visitCount+1, calls saveBookmark(updated), then opens the URL with window.open(item.url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer').

The displayed list filters by isArchived matching the active tab, requires every selected tag to be present in bookmark.tags, matches search only against bookmark.title.toLowerCase(), and sorts pinned-first then by the chosen sort mode with createdAt descending as fallback.
The Archive/Unarchive action toggles isArchived and, when archiving, forces isPinned=false before saving.
Tag counts are derived by iterating all in-memory bookmarks and counting each tag occurrence, then sorted alphabetically for the sidebar.
Retrieval by keyword covers only bookmark titles, not URLs, descriptions, or tag names, so the scenario's 'find by a remembered word' workflow is partially supported.

The app supports the scenario's save-now/find-later loop: a deliberate add dialog writes a URL-anchored record into durable IndexedDB, and the record can later be browsed, tag-filtered, title-searched, and opened back to the live URL.

fetchMeta calls https://api.microlink.io/?url=... and, on success with result.data, sets title/description and fetches the logo through https://images.weserv.nl/; errors are only console.error'd and the finally block resets loading.

case_design.capability: F08: a single-user personal library persisted in SQLite that survives browser sessions and server restarts, with records queried from the database for every request rather than held in a browser store.
case_design.reason: The evidence shows Dexie writes on save/delete and a one-time db.bookmarks.toArray() hydration into an in-memory RippleMap, scoped to one browser profile with no sync. The target adopts local, single-user, cross-session retention but replaces IndexedDB/Dexie and in-memory hydration with SQLite on the Python server; it does not claim browser-profile persistence, multi-device sync, or the source map as target design.

case_design.capability: F11: the library is delivered as Python server-rendered HTML pages and forms using POST/redirect/GET for saving records, managing categories, moving records between categories, and soft-delete/restore, including a ready empty-library view. P0 has no standalone record-editing page; record URL updates retain only the existing PATCH /api/bookmarks/{id} contract.
case_design.reason: The evidence describes a client-mounted SPA: Edit is an in-page dialog populated from item fields, and component creation loads Dexie rows into a client RippleMap. The target implements the already-declared P0 save, category-management, move and soft-delete/restore journeys as Python 3.12 HTML responses. Source SPA mounting, client-side dialog state and Dexie hydration are not carried over. The source Edit dialog does not imply a target record-editing UI; the existing PATCH API retains URL updates and recomputes hostname when the URL changes. The save-now/find-later loop and ready empty state remain the target intent.

case_design.capability: A deliberate save creates a URL-anchored record with a stable id, a locally derived hostname, creation time and initial active state. Later changes preserve the record id and creation time; updating the URL recomputes hostname from the new URL. The adopted capability is this identity and creation lifecycle; visitCount and visitedAt are not target fields or P0 obligations.
case_design.reason: The accepted observation records the source's bm-prefixed UUID identity, hostname derivation, createdAt, initial flags and visit fields, and preservation of identity and creation/visit fields on edit. These remain source observations. The target adopts stable record identity and creation time, represented by its existing id/created_at model and made durable by SQLite; it does not import the source's visitCount/visitedAt fields, which F24 excludes. URL updates follow the existing PATCH contract and derive hostname again. The source's tag constraints and other state fields are not silently imported into the category or target data model.

case_design.capability: URL validation accepts only absolute, parseable HTTP(S) URLs with a nonempty valid hostname, allows single-label hosts such as http://localhost, preserves the original URL text, and rejects malformed, non-HTTP(S) or empty-host input without writing; no DNS or online-reachability check is performed.
case_design.reason: The upstream Valibot rule is a dotted-host regex that requires a dot-separated domain and an alphabetic top-level suffix, so it rejects localhost. That regex is retained as a source fact and mapped as adjusted, not reused as the target rule: the target parses the URL, checks the http/https scheme, absolute form and hostname presence, permits single-label hosts, and stores the entered string unchanged.

case_design.capability: Create, rename and delete named categories with validation and with protection or reassignment when a category still contains records, assign one at save time, move records between categories, and default uncategorized saves into an Inbox category.
case_design.reason: Evidence shows the source has no category entity: classification is only up to five free-text tags, there is no collection CRUD or separate move, and the form rejects saves with zero tags. The target therefore designs first-class categories, an inbox default for unclassified capture and an explicit move action; these are new target concepts, not source-derived tag behavior.

case_design.capability: Browse one category and see only its active records, with a category count that agrees with the listed records after adds, moves and restores.
case_design.reason: Source facts derive tag counts by scanning all in-memory bookmarks and filter records by requiring every selected tag. The target computes category counts and category-scoped lists in SQL over active, non-deleted rows so the count and the list stay consistent; the source tag-sidebar algorithm is not the target implementation.

case_design.capability: Search the selected category by keyword across title, hostname and description using case-insensitive substring matching, retaining category and query and rendering matching or explicit empty results.
case_design.reason: Source search lowercases and compares only bookmark.title; the fixed target F06/A07 contract adjusts it to title, derived hostname and description, combined with the selected category. Raw URL text, category names and tags are not additional keyword fields. This clarifies target design only; accepted observations, evidence IDs, source revision and disposition remain unchanged.

case_design.capability: Open a saved record as a navigation to its stored original URL, preserving the URL text and never fetching, proxying or prefetching the destination during save, listing or open preparation.
case_design.reason: Source opens the URL with window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') after updating visit state. The target renders the record URL as an ordinary HTTP(S) link or server redirect with the same new-tab/no-referrer intent; opening is a user navigation distinct from saving, and the Python server does not request the target page.

case_design.capability: Do not enrich saved records with third-party metadata or favicon services and do not prefetch saved target pages; stored title, description and URL come from the user or local derivation.
case_design.reason: The source calls api.microlink.io and images.weserv.nl/Google s2 favicons on save and treats failures as silent. The target P0 deliberately omits these outbound calls because saving and opening must remain distinct from fetching; no target-page response, metadata or icon is retrieved, and no source enrichment behavior is presented as target design.

case_design.capability: Soft-delete an active record into a recoverable trash and restore it later, instead of allowing deletion only on archived items with a transient toast undo.
case_design.reason: Source facts limit Delete to archived items and provide recovery only through an Undo action on the toast, with no trash view and no deletion path for active records. The target uses an explicit soft-delete/restore lifecycle exposed in HTML so records remain recoverable; this changes the source's archived-only and transient-recovery model.

acceptance: 计划页对每个分配项同时显示计划金额、实际金额与剩余额度，并在录入支出后立即更新
任何一笔支出录入后，其所属分配项的剩余额度按该支出金额减少
分配项的实际支出超过计划金额后，其剩余额度显示为负数或明确的超支标记，而不是归零或隐藏
从分配项 A 转移金额到分配项 B 后，A 的剩余减少额与 B 的剩余增加额相同，计划总额不变
进入下一期后各分配项的计划金额回到模板数值，上一期剩余不被带入（未启用结转时）
scenario.audience: 希望用预先承诺约束日常开支、且不连接银行账户的个人用户（如刚独立生活的年轻上班族）
scenario.name: 个人极简月度预算：先查剩余再消费
scenario.objective: 为一个月的各项用途预先设定计划金额，并在每次消费前查看该用途的剩余额度，让计划真正影响消费决策。
workflow: 新建本期（月度）计划，为食品、房租、交通、娱乐等用途创建分配项并填写计划金额
登记本期可用的预期收入，检查各分配项计划金额之和是否超过收入
消费后手动录入一笔支出并归属到对应分配项，该分配项剩余额度随即减少
购买前打开计划页，查看相关分配项及整体的剩余额度，据此决定是否购买或缩减金额
月中某分配项即将用尽，从其他分配项转移金额，或让超出部分留在该分配项上形成超支
期末查看各分配项的计划、实际与剩余对照，未使用金额留在本期，并按模板数值开始下一期计划
